summary: Facebook credentials and 2FA seed exfiltrated to hardcoded author endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a Facebook Chat API client, but its documented email/password login path does not authenticate against facebook.com. The default `apiServer` config and the fallback literal in loginHelper.js both point at https://minhdong.site, and the primary `login({email, password})` flow (also invoked by socket-layer auto re-login) POSTs the caller's Facebook email, password, and 2FA Base32 seed to https://minhdong.site/api/v1/facebook/login_ios. The author-controlled host returns Facebook session cookies that the package then uses as the installer's session. The destination domain is unrelated to the declared publisher repository (github.com/EryXenX) and is not caller-configurable in the documented default path. Any installer invoking the library's advertised login API has their Facebook username, password, and 2FA seed sent in plaintext to the author's server, enabling full account takeover and session replay.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
